memories.memory: I keep about $42,000 in an emergency savings account and try not to touch it, even when unexpected expenses come up.
After retiring from my community outreach job in 2021, my monthly pension and Social Security together dropped my income to roughly $3,800 before taxes.
In October 2023, I invested $8,000 in a former colleague's small home-care business because I believed in her plan, although the money is still tied up.
I put a $6,500 roof repair on a low-interest credit line last spring and am paying it down with $275 monthly payments.
My daughter borrowed $2,400 from me for a professional certification course, and we agreed she would repay it in small installments whenever her budget allows.
I receive a modest annuity payment from an old employer every month, but I have not yet decided whether to leave it invested or use it for travel.
Last year I discovered that an unfamiliar $186 charge had appeared on my credit card, so I froze the card and moved most of my automatic payments to a replacement account.
